breaking: 🚨 UN DAY: Donald Trump begins a major programme of meetings in New York covering Iran, Ukraine, Gulf security, Canada, Denmark and Greenland.

🇺🇸🇮🇷 US–IRAN: Markets are watching for possible diplomatic movement at the UN. Brent crude has fallen towards $98 after reports raised hopes of increased Gulf supply and possible reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
🛢️ Saudi Aramco has resumed stronger crude exports through Gulf terminals, with about 14 million barrels loaded onto seven supertankers on Sunday.
🇫🇷🇺🇦🇷🇺 UKRAINE: Emmanuel Macron says he discussed with Trump a possible moratorium on attacks against energy infrastructure in Russia and Ukraine. No energy truce has been agreed.
🇨🇦🇪🇺 CANADA–EU: The proposed associate-member relationship remains under discussion. Canada is not joining the EU, and the proposed status has no established EU treaty framework.
🇺🇸🇨🇳 US–CHINA: Trade, tariffs, AI and critical minerals remain central to Washington–Beijing discussions ahead of the Trump–Xi summit.
🤖 AI SECURITY: Chinese AI company DeepSeek is expected to brief the UN Security Council this week on artificial-intelligence risks alongside representatives from OpenAI and Anthropic.
🇬🇧🏭 UK: INEOS says it will mothball three chemical plants in Hull because of high European gas prices. The sites employ nearly 4,000 people.
✈️ EUROPE: The continent faces a projected fourth-quarter jet-fuel deficit of about 510,000 barrels per day, with South Korea becoming an increasingly important supplier.
🇳🇬 NIGERIA: Dangote Refinery is attracting more fuel buyers as imported petrol and diesel become more expensive than its reported domestic selling prices.
🇳🇬 DANGOTE IPO: Strong retail demand has overwhelmed several Nigerian investment platforms, highlighting both investor interest and pressure on fintech infrastructure.
🌍 AFRICA: Dangote's refinery has become an increasingly important supplier of refined fuel to Europe during the global energy disruption.

featured.title: Trump's UN Diplomacy Puts Iran and Ukraine at Centre of Global Attention
featured.content: Donald Trump is in New York for an intensive programme of diplomatic meetings on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly. His agenda includes discussions involving Iran, Ukraine, Gulf states, Denmark and Greenland. The Middle East remains particularly important because the conflict has disrupted energy markets and international shipping, while the Ukraine war continues to threaten European energy security ahead of winter. Trump is also expected to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as diplomatic efforts continue.
featured.imageQuery: Trump United Nations General Assembly New York diplomacy

articles.title: Oil Markets React to Possible US–Iran Diplomatic Movement
articles.content: Oil prices have become highly sensitive to developments between Washington and Tehran. Brent crude fell towards $98 per barrel after reports suggested that Iran may be prepared to discuss conditions for diplomacy and that the Strait of Hormuz could potentially see increased traffic if military pressure eases. The market remains cautious because refined-product supplies, particularly diesel, remain tight. Any sustained diplomatic progress could reduce the geopolitical risk premium, but no final agreement has been reached.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Increases Gulf Oil Shipments
articles.content: Saudi Aramco has increased crude shipments from Gulf terminals following earlier disruptions to Saudi export infrastructure. Tanker-tracking data showed around 14 million barrels loaded onto seven supertankers inside the Gulf on Sunday. The additional shipments are helping maintain international supply while the regional security situation remains uncertain.
articles.imageQuery: Saudi Aramco supertanker Gulf oil export

articles.title: Macron Discusses Possible Ukraine–Russia Energy Moratorium
articles.content: French President Emmanuel Macron says he discussed with Donald Trump the possibility of establishing a moratorium on attacks against energy infrastructure in Ukraine and Russia. Macron also stressed the need for additional air-defence interceptors for Ukraine. The proposal could help protect power and energy infrastructure ahead of winter, but there is currently no confirmed Russia–Ukraine energy truce.

articles.title: Canada–EU Associate-Member Proposal Remains Under Discussion
articles.content: The European Commission's proposal to explore an associate-member relationship for Canada continues to attract international attention. Canada already has a major trade relationship with Europe, but the proposed arrangement could extend cooperation into defence, energy, critical minerals, AI, space, telecommunications, research and investment. Canada is not becoming a full EU member, and the proposed status would require negotiations because there is no established EU treaty category defining it.

articles.title: Trump's UN Meetings Include Iran, Ukraine, Gulf and Greenland
articles.content: Donald Trump is holding a series of meetings with international leaders during the UN General Assembly. His programme includes discussions with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Gulf leaders and representatives from Denmark and Greenland. Iran and the wider Middle East conflict are expected to remain central to the discussions because of their effects on energy prices and shipping security.
articles.imageQuery: Trump UN meetings world leaders New York

articles.title: DeepSeek Set to Brief UN Security Council on AI Risks
articles.content: Chinese AI company DeepSeek is expected to brief the United Nations Security Council this week on risks associated with artificial intelligence. Representatives from OpenAI and Anthropic are also expected to participate. The Security Council meeting will examine how increasingly powerful AI systems could affect international security, governance and human control. The development reflects the growing shift of AI from a technology-policy issue into the international-security arena.
articles.imageQuery: DeepSeek AI United Nations Security Council artificial intelligence

articles.title: US–China AI Competition Expands Beyond Business
articles.content: Artificial intelligence has become an increasingly important part of US–China relations. Washington and Beijing are discussing AI safety alongside broader disagreements involving semiconductors, trade and critical minerals. The two countries are also preparing for a leaders' summit in Washington, where technology and supply chains are expected to feature prominently.
articles.imageQuery: US China artificial intelligence technology competition

articles.title: INEOS to Suspend Three Hull Chemical Plants Over Energy Costs
articles.content: British chemicals company INEOS says it will suspend operations at three plants in Hull because of high European gas prices. The affected sites employ nearly 4,000 people and produce chemicals used in medicines, cosmetics, clothing, detergents and construction materials. Reuters reports that UK gas prices are dramatically higher than US benchmark prices, highlighting the competitiveness challenge facing energy-intensive European industry.
articles.imageQuery: INEOS Hull chemical plant UK industry

articles.title: Europe Faces Major Fourth-Quarter Jet-Fuel Supply Deficit
articles.content: Europe is expected to face a jet-fuel supply deficit of roughly 510,000 barrels per day during the fourth quarter of 2026. Disruption to Middle Eastern supplies has forced European buyers to look further afield. South Korea has become a major supplier, with September shipments to Europe reaching their highest level since October 2022. Lower European jet-fuel inventories are adding to concerns about aviation costs.
articles.imageQuery: European airport jet fuel aircraft refuelling

articles.title: Dangote Refinery Gains Domestic Market Advantage
articles.content: Nigeria's Dangote Refinery continues to attract fuel purchases from local marketers as estimated import-parity prices rise above the refinery's reported selling prices. Greater domestic refining capacity could reduce Nigeria's dependence on imported petroleum products while the international market remains under pressure. Dangote is also expanding its refinery from approximately 700,000 barrels per day towards 1.4 million barrels per day.

articles.title: Dangote IPO Tests Nigeria's Digital Investment Infrastructure
articles.content: The Dangote Petroleum Refinery IPO has attracted unusually strong retail investor interest, with several Nigerian digital investment platforms experiencing outages during periods of heavy demand. The offer involves 4.1 billion shares at ₦525 each and targets about ₦2.15 trillion. Regulators have warned investors to verify authorised platforms and avoid fraudulent schemes impersonating the IPO.

articles.title: Dangote Refinery Increasingly Important to European Fuel Market
articles.content: Dangote Refinery has become an increasingly significant supplier of refined petroleum products to Europe during the disruption of Middle Eastern fuel flows. Its exports include jet fuel and diesel, giving Nigeria a larger role in the international refined-products market. The development also highlights the growing connection between Nigerian refining capacity and European energy security.
articles.imageQuery: Dangote refinery fuel exports Europe tanker

articles.title: Energy Security, Trade and Technology Become Increasingly Connected
articles.content: Three major forces are increasingly influencing the global economy at the same time: energy security, trade policy and technology competition. The Middle East is affecting oil and shipping costs, US–China tensions are reshaping technology supply chains, and Europe is developing new strategic relationships with countries such as Canada. For businesses and consumers, geopolitical decisions can ultimately influence prices, investment, employment and the availability of goods.

morningSummary: Good afternoon. Global attention is focused on Donald Trump's diplomatic programme at the United Nations, where Iran, Ukraine, Gulf security and Greenland are among the major issues. Oil markets have eased as investors assess possible US–Iran diplomacy, although refined fuel supplies remain tight. Emmanuel Macron is also discussing a possible moratorium on attacks against Russian and Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Canada and the EU continue to explore a proposed associate-member relationship, while artificial intelligence moves deeper into international security discussions as DeepSeek prepares to brief the UN Security Council. In Europe, high gas prices are forcing INEOS to suspend three Hull chemical plants, while the continent faces a significant fourth-quarter jet-fuel supply deficit. In Nigeria, Dangote Refinery remains central to both domestic fuel supply and international refined-product markets.
bigQuestion: As energy security, artificial intelligence, trade and defence increasingly shape international partnerships, are countries entering a new era where economic security is becoming just as important as military security?
